L33: ### A
L34: 
L35:   * Adjustable Shock Absorbers
L36: 
L37:     * Rear shock absorbers that provide load leveling without a host of moving parts or an on board air compressor
L38:     * Internal shock valving senses ride height and uses energy from the vehicle’s motion to increase hydraulic pressure and raise the shock to the desired ride level
L39:     * As the vehicle is driven, the shocks quickly “pump up” to the necessary pressure, and the vehicle’s original ride level is restored
L40:   * Aerodynamic Drag
L41:     * Drag or resistance produced by a moving object, such as a motor vehicle, as it displaces the air in its path
L42:     * Usually measured in pounds, aerodynamic drag increases in proportion to an object’s frontal area, drag coefficient and the square of its speed
L43:   * Air Dam
L44:     * Soft, lower body extension attached below the front bumper improving vehicle performance by limiting the amount of airflow directed under the vehicle
L45:     * Improves aerodynamics and redirects the airflow to the engine compartment for improved engine cooling or air conditioning performance
L46:     * Assists in reducing aerodynamic lift, turbulence and drag
L47:   * Air Dryer
L48:     * A component of the air conditioning system
L49:     * Condenses and filters moisture and contaminants from pressurized air from the air compressor
L50:     * Most air dryers use a drying agent known as a desiccant to remove moisture from the air
L51:     * Moisture is automatically expelled when the compressor unloads
L52:   * Air Suspension Seat
L53:     * Single seat, either driver or passenger, which incorporates an air-activated suspension system to help eliminate the jolts and bounces of the truck cab
L54:     * Note: Normally air suspension seats require that the truck be equipped with air brakes to supply air to the seat
L55:     * Some seats feature an integral air compressor so the occupant can energize the seat on vehicles that are not equipped with air brakes
L56:   * Air/Fuel Mixture
L57:     * The measure or ratio of the amounts of air and fuel being fed to the engine’s cylinders. The power train control module (PCM) computer adjusts the air/fuel mixture to provide the best combination of performance and fuel efficiency
L58:     * A higher percentage of fuel to air is described as a rich mixture, while a lower percentage of fuel to air is termed a lean mixture
L59:     * On Ford vehicles, the air/fuel mixture is measured by an electronic sensor that provides input to the power train control module systems
L60:   * Airbag
L61:     * During a moderate-to-severe frontal impact, the airbag is designed to inflate in approximately 1/20th of a second (less time than it takes to blink an eye) and begins to deflate immediately thereafter. In that brief period, the airbag can help reduce the risk of injury to the head and chest of the driver and/or the right front seat passenger
L62:     * Electronic diagnostic module continuously monitors the airbag for proper operation
L63:     * When the ignition switch is turned to the ON position, the airbag indicator light on the instrument cluster illuminates for approximately six seconds to signal that the system is functioning properly. Should a fault occur in the system, the airbag indicator light flashes, stays on or fails to illuminate when the ignition switch is turned to the Start position. This signifies immediate service is required
L64:     * Always put small children and child seats in the rear seating positions (except jump seats). Deactivate the passenger airbag with the airbag shutoff switch (if equipped) when using a rear-facing child safety seat in the front passenger seat
L65:     * Dual-stage Airbags
L66:     * Can deploy at two different levels, or nor at all, depending on the information sent to the Restraint Control Module from various sensors located within the vehicle
L67:     * In less severe collision events, the airbags will deploy in the lower or first stage of deployment force
L68:     * In more severe collision events, airbags will deploy at both stages or at full force
L69:     * Seat sensors, in some front passenger seats, can detect the weight of passengers and deploy only if the occupant is above a certain weightSecond Generation Airbags
L70:     * Designed to inflate with less force than that employed in earlier or first generation designs
L71:     * The airbags reduce the peak inflation pressure and/or rise rate
L72:     * Rise rate is the force and speed with which an airbag inflates and is controlled by factors such as the type and amount of inflator gas, the actual airbag size and the design of the vent used to release the pressure from the airbag once deployed
L73:     * Note: The airbag is not a substitute for safety belts. Safety belts must be properly worn at all times to maximize the effectiveness of the system. Always secure children in the back seat (except jump seats).
L74:   * All-Wheel Drive (AWD)
L75:     * Continuously monitors wheel speed, throttle position and steering-wheel angle sensors to determine the vehicle’s conditions and driver’s intent. The system then determines the optimal amount of front and rear torque for the given conditions to not only reduce wheel slip but to prevent the slip from occurring in the first place
L76:     * Helps ensure the vehicle will be sure-footed on the road in a variety of conditions, such as fast cornering, uneven pavement, potholes, slippery surfaces and anything that compromises traction
L77:     * Vehicle normally functions in front-wheel-drive mode
L78:     * When sensors detect that wheel slip is occurring or even just likely to occur, the All-Wheel-Drive (AWD) system can react within as little as 50 milliseconds to distribute up to 100 percent of the available torque to the rear wheels
L79:     * Controller may detect a difference in wheel speed front-to-rear even in good weather, such as when driving through sand, mud or wet leaves
L80:     * How the System Works
L81:     * All-Wheel Drive uses electromagnetic activation of an internal clutch pack
L82:     * Engages when sensors detect wheel slip in the front wheels, and often acts preemptively to prevent slip from happening in the first place
L83:     * When activated, the system uses force from an electromagnet to push clutch plates together
L84:     * Drive shaft torque is transmitted through the unit to the rear wheels, taking power from the front wheel sand sending it to the rear
L85:     * Benefits of the System
L86:     * No driver interaction is required to activate AWD. It’s there when your customers need it
L87:     * The system can send up to 100 percent of the engine’s torque to front or rear as needed to avoid wheel slip
L88:     * Operates with speed and sophistication to help provide peace of mind and driving confidence
L89:     * Releases just as quickly, avoiding binding or wheel skid once traction improves
L90:     * Benefits on either wet or dry pavement. Because the system can transfer torque quickly away from the front wheels, it helps reduce the type of understeer often associated with front-wheel-drive vehicles to provide improved vehicle control
L91:     * Lightweight with few moving parts, for little impact on fuel economy
L92:     * When AWD is combined with All-Speed Traction Control or the AdvanceTrac® system, a high degree of torque can be sent to the wheel with the best traction, even if the other three wheels have no traction at all
L93:   * Alternative Fuel Vehicle (also see E85 Vehicles and Flexible Fuel Vehicle (FFV))
L94:     * Refers to any type of vehicle that uses nontraditional fuel or power sources:
L95:     * Methanol/Ethanol
L96:     * Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)
L97:     * Propane
L98:     * Electricity (as in Escape Hybrid)
L99:   * Alternator
L100:     * Engine-driven device that converts mechanical energy into alternating electrical current
L101:     * Provides power to run all of the vehicle’s electrical components when the engine is running
L102:     * Single or dual heavy-duty alternators that provide additional charging capacity are also available for applications such as cold-climate operation (temperatures below -20°F) where battery drain and accessory use are typically very high, and vehicles are equipped for towing purposes
L103:   * Alternator Capacity
L104:     * To determine minimum capacity for an alternator:
L105:     * Minimum alternator output = Total load x 1.20, where total load comprises continuous night-winter load
L106:     * Add 20 percent (.20) to accommodate anticipated intermittent load
L107:     * In most cases, a 2.51:1 or better alternator drive ratio will provide a reasonably adequate system output
L108:   * Ambient Interior Lighting
L109:     * Utilizes Light-Emitting Diode (LED) lights to illuminate the vehicle interior: foot wells, cup holders, and controls, depending upon the vehicle
L110:     * Offers the ability to change color to suit your mood. Color selections include aqua, blue, green, purple, red, yellow or white lighting
L111:   * Anti-theft Systems
L112:     * Perimeter anti-theft alarm system
L113:     * Guards the vehicle's doors, hood and trunk/lift gate. When an unauthorized entry occurs, the system trigger sand will:– Flash the head lamps, parking lamps and theft-indicator lamp on the instrument panel
L114:     * Sound the horn. Note: It will not be triggered by breaking glass or entry into the vehicle through a window. The perimeter anti-theft alarm system is designed to work with the factory-installed Remote Keyless Entry System. SecuriLock® passive anti-theft ignition system
L115:     * Uses a sophisticated electronically coded ignition key to start the vehicle. The system is designed to help prevent the engine from being started unless a coded key programmed to the vehicle is used. There is no battery on the key itself; the small amount of energy required to identify the key is supplied by the vehicle
L116:     * SecuriLock is designed so that it is not necessary for the driver to follow any procedure to arm the system. It is automatically armed when the key is removed from the ignition and is disarmed when the key is reinserted into the ignition
L117:     * Spare keys will be available from dealerships. Customers can program their keys by using each original (2) key in the proper sequence and finally inserting a new key for programming (see Owner's Guide for more details)
L118:     * There are billions of possible codes
L119:   * Auto lamp System
L120:     * Provides ambient-light-sensitive automatic on-off control of the exterior lights normally controlled by the head lamp control switch
L121:     * Comes preprogrammed to keep the lights on for approximately 20 seconds after the ignition switch is turned off
L122:     * If desired, the time delay can be reprogrammed on some vehicles to keep the lights on for up to 3 minutes after the ignition is turned off. See the vehicle Owner’s Guide for more details
L123:   * Auto lock
L124:     * Auto lock feature will lock all the doors, lift gate and lift gate window when all doors are closed, the ignition is in the ON position, the vehicle is shifted into any drive gear putting the vehicle in motion
L125:     * See the vehicle Owner’s Guide for vehicle-specific information on the range of functions
L126:   * Auxiliary Springs
L127:     * Used on many light trucks for load stability or to support heavy loads with minimal effect on ride characteristics
L128:     * Help control roll and sway of trucks with high bodies that carry loads that might shift when cornering or operating on high-crowned roads
L129:     * Usually used on rear leaf springs, and are mounted to act only after the regular springs are partially deflected under heavy loads
L130:   * Axle Ratio
L131:     * The number of output shaft (on front-wheel-drive vehicles) or drive shaft (on rear-wheel-drive vehicles) revolutions required to rotate the axle one full turn
L132:     * For a rear-wheel-drive vehicle with an axle ratio of 3.55:1, the drive shaft would have to rotate 3.55 times to rotate the rear axle once. This is also known as the Final Drive Ratio
L133:     * Lower numeric axle ratios tend to be more fuel-efficient. Higher axle ratios deliver added torque for increased power for acceleration and trailer towing
L134:     * Front-wheel-drive vehicles employ an Axle Transfer Ratio, essentially a Final Drive Ratio
L135:   * Axle, 2-speed
L136:     * Type of rear drive axle offering two reduction ratios and a control mechanism for selecting either ratio at the driver’s discretion
L137:     * "Lo" axle range (the higher numerical ratio) provides maximum pulling power
L138:     * "Hi" range (the lower numerical ratio) provides maximum road speed
L139:     * 2-speed rear axle permits split-shifting in the lower transmission gears to obtain evenly spaced gear steps that optimize available engine power
L140:     * 2-speed axle can be used in Lo range for crisp performance at slower speeds or in Hi range for maximum economy on the highway
L141:   * Axles, Rear Drive
L142:     * Full-floating Rear Axle — Generally used in heavier-duty applications. The full-floating axle shafts “float” within the outer axle housing where they drive the wheels. The outer housing supports the entire rear weight through double-opposed wheel bearings, which absorb all load and wheel stress
L143:     * Semi-floating Rear Axle — The axle shafts and wheel bearings not only support the total weight, but also transmit driving torque to the wheels. This axle system also resists stress due to skidding, turning corners and other traction forces
L144:     * See Live Axle for more information
L145: ### B
L146: 
L147:   * Balance Shaft
L148: 
L149:     * Engine shaft designed so it rotates in a way that reduces or cancels out vibrations produced by the engine, resulting in reduced noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) in the passenger compartment
L150:     * In 4-cylinder engines, two shafts turning in opposite directions on either side of the engine’s crankshaft are generally used, while in V-type engines, a single balance shaft is used
L151:   * Battery Saver
L152: Feature on some vehicles that automatically turns off interior or under hood lights after a set period of time (e.g., 30–45 minutes), to help prevent battery power drainage and save enough power to restart the vehicle.
L153: 
L154:   * Bio-foam Seat Materials
L155:     * Type of foam used in Mustang and Escape/Escape Hybrid seat production
L156:     * Production of bio-foam is designed to emit less carbon dioxide into the atmosphere
L157:     * Material is designed to require less energy to produce than the petroleum-based foam
L158:     * Emphasizes Ford’s commitment to its environmental responsibility
L159:   * Body-on-frame Construction
L160:     * Type of vehicle construction with the body attached to a separate frame, often with rubber mounts to reduce squeaks and rattles, helping to isolate road noise and vibration
L161:     * Typically more sturdy and robust when compared to vehicles with unibody construction
L162:     * Provides a solid foundation that contributes to payload and towing capability
L163:   * Bore and Stroke
L164:     * While these two terms are frequently used together, they are two totally different measurements
L165:     * Bore is the measurement of the inside diameter of a cylinder
L166:     * Stroke is the distance the piston travels from top-dead-center (TDC) to bottom-dead-center (BDC) of the cylinder
L167:   * Box Side Steps
L168:     * Frame-mounted steps located on each side of the truck cargo box and in front of the rear wheel well used to make it easy to access the cargo box. Able to support up to 500 lbs.
L169:     * Allow convenient side access to the cargo box using a release lever located on the step
L170:     * Return to stowage position by pushing the steps back into/under the cargo box
L171:   * Boxed Frame
L172: As the name implies, a "boxed" frame has four sides, which provides additional strength. It is a closed structural section that has greater resistance to twisting and torsion forces than comparably sized "open" frame designs.
L173: 
L174:   * Brake Bias
L175: 
L176: Front/rear distribution of a vehicle’s braking power. Generally the front of a vehicle where the engine and majority of weight and steering functions are located supplies the greater amount of braking power.
L177: 
L178:   * Brake Modulation
L179: The process of varying pedal pressure to hold a vehicle on the verge of lockup to supply maximum braking efficiency. Anti-lock Braking Systems (ABS) employ computer-controlled modulators to maximize braking efficiency.
L180: 
L181:   * Brake/Shift Interlock (Automatic Transmissions)
L182:     * Requires driver to depress the brake pedal in order to shift out of Park and into any gear
L183:     * Prevents accidental engagement of drive gears
L184:     * Vehicles with a floor-mounted gearshift lever include a manual override in the console; vehicles with a column-mounted gearshift include a manual override under the steering column
L185:   * Braking Systems
L186:     * Ford Motor Company uses a number of different braking systems on its passenger cars, crossovers, SUVs and light trucks, including the following: Four-wheel Anti-lock Braking System (ABS)
L187:     * Helps provide straight, more controlled stops, while helping the driver maintain steering control undermost road conditions, including slippery road surfaces
L188:     * ABS computer-controlled sensors prevent wheels from locking up, even when the driver presses hard on the brake pedal
L189:     * Sensors continuously monitor the speed of each wheel. When impending wheel lockup is detected, the computer signals the hydraulic control unit to apply and release (automatically “pumping”) the brakes several times per second with split-second timing, providing a level of braking efficiency that even professional race car drivers cannot duplicate and resulting in shorter stopping distances and greater braking and steering control
L190:     * Three-channel ABS
L191:     * Uses three individual channels to monitor and control brake pressure to the front wheels individually and to both rear wheels together
L192:     * Four-channel ABS
L193:     * Operates similarly to the three-channel system, except that both rear wheels are monitored and operated separately
L194:     * ABS Functionality
L195:     * Computer continuously monitors the ABS for malfunctions. Should a problem develop, an instrument panel light alerts the driver that the ABS computer has shut down and the brakes have been returned to normal, non-ABS operation
L196:     * Driver should never pump the brakes in a vehicle equipped with ABS. This defeats the system and increases stopping distances. For best performance, the driver should apply maximum pedal pressure
L197:     * When using ABS, the driver may feel a slight pulsing sensation; this is completely normal
L198:     * Dual Diagonal Braking System
L199:     * All Ford vehicles feature either a diagonal or front-rear split hydraulic brake system with warning lamp (excluding F-650/F-750 with air brakes)
L200:     * With this system, diagonal circuits link front and rear wheels at opposite corners, so braking capacity is retained even if one of the two circuits malfunctions
L201:     * Power-assisted Four-wheel Disc Brakes
L202:     * Four-wheel disc brakes consist of a disc at each wheel that rotates at wheel speed and is straddled by a caliper that squeezes the inner and outer faces of the disc to provide stopping or braking power
L203:     * Disc brakes provide a more linear response, and therefore operate more efficiently at high temperatures than drum brakes
L204:     * Power-assisted disc brakes use a vacuum-assist to provide power to the master cylinder, thereby greatly reducing pedal effort
L205:     * Ford power-assisted disc brakes are self-adjusting with pad clearance automatically maintained by the limited retracting action of the piston in the caliper Power-assisted Front Disc/Rear Drum Brakes Combination of the front disc and rear drum brake system. Drum brakes are a type of brake that has an iron casting shaped like a shallow drum that rotates with the wheel. Curved brake shoes are forced into contact with the inner face of the drum to provide stopping or braking power.
L206: Power-assisted drum brakes use a vacuum-assist to provide power to the master cylinder, thereby greatly reducing pedal effort. Features of this system include:
L207:     * Front disc brake pad clearance automatically maintained by the limited retracting action of the piston in the caliper
L208:     * Adjustment of the rear drum brakes is accomplished when the brake pedal is applied while the vehicle is moving in Reverse
L209:     * Both front and rear brakes are self-adjusting
L210:     * Note: Availability of braking systems varies according to model. Refer to the individual vehicle sections of the 2009Source Books or to the Ordering Guide for specific availability.
L211:   * Breakaway Valve
L212: Safety valve designed to protect the air supply of a tractor or leading trailer and automatically apply the brakes of a trailing unit in the event of accidental separation.
L213: ### C
L214: 
L215:   * Cam Profile
L216: 
L217: Shape of each lobe on a camshaft that determines the amount or duration of time an intake or exhaust valve is open and the valve’s maximum opening, or "lift."
L218: 
L219:   * Camber
L220: 
L221: Inclination of the plane of a wheel to the vertical plane of symmetry of a vehicle.
L222: 
L223:   * Camshaft
L224: 
L225: Shaft in an engine block or cylinder head that includes a series of lobes which regulates opening and closing the intake and exhaust valves, allowing the engine to "breathe."
L226: 
L227:   * Cargo Management Rails
L228:     * Two aluminum rails attached to the upper rail of a cargo box
L229:     * Include four adjustable tie-down cleats that can be positioned along the cargo box rails, providing secure attachment points to keep cargo in place
L230:   * Cargo Tie-down Net
L231: 
L232:     * Usually made of nylon mesh
L233:     * Secures cargo and packages in a vehicle's luggage compartment or rear cargo area
L234:   * Caster
L235: The angle between the steering axis and the true vertical axis when viewed from the side. Caster is considered "positive" when the steering axis is inclined upward and toward the rear.
L236: 
L237:   * Catalytic Converter
L238:     * Muffler-shaped device in the exhaust system
L239:     * Usually contains platinum, palladium and/or rhodium, which acts as a catalyst in a chemical reaction that converts unburned hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen into water vapor, carbon dioxide and other gases that are less toxic than untreated exhaust fumes
L240:   * Center Differential
L241: 
L242: Used in some four-wheel-drive vehicles to distribute power to the front and rear differentials.
L243: 
L244:   * Center of Gravity (Center of Mass)
L245: Point at which the entire weight of a body is considered to be concentrated so that, if supported at this point, the body would remain in equilibrium in any position.
L246: 
L247:   * Charge Motion Control Valves
L248:     * Electronically controlled metal flap located at the end of each intake runner
L249:     * These flaps are specially shaped to speed up the intake charge at low engine speed and induce a tumble effecting the combustion chamber that results in a more thorough fuel/air mixture and quicker, more efficient burn
L250:     * At higher engine speed the flaps are completely open and do not affect the intake charge
L251:   * Chassis
L252:     * Portion of the vehicle that includes:
L253:     * Suspension
L254:     * Steering components
L255:     * Power train
L256:     * Brakes
L257:     * Fuel system Refer to the Power trains section of this book for details concerning Ford power train systems.
L258:   * Chassis Cab
L259:     * Unfinished truck featuring an occupant compartment, or cab, without a cargo bed
L260:     * A chassis cab requires the addition of cargo-carrying (cargo box, flatbed), work-performing (tow lift) or load-bearing (dump assembly) components to perform its intended functions
L261:   * Climate-controlled Seats
L262:     * Feature a tiny thermoelectric device that allows the occupant to cool or warm the seat and backrest depending on outdoor temperature and personal preference
L263:     * The thermoelectric modules are solid-state devices with surfaces that turn hot or cold depending on the polarity of the applied direct current electricity
L264:     * Heat-transfer components attached to the modules cool or heat the air that is blown past them and then is circulated through ducts and pads in the seats and onto the occupants
L265:     * Each seat has individual electronic controls to adjust the level of cooling or heating desired
L266:   * Clutch
L267:     * Mechanical device that engages and disengages the engine from the transmission/Trans axle during shifting, operated by a pedal to the left of the brake pedal
L268:     * Depressing the clutch pedal interrupts power flow to the transmission/Trans axle. Releasing the clutch pedal with the gearshift in place will reengage the transmission/trans axle
L269:     * Clutch must be fully depressed to start a vehicle with a manual transmission/transaxle
L270:   * Coil Spring
L271: Spiral-shaped spring that can be compressed or extended without permanent deformation and that is widely used in front and rear suspension systems, including the Macpherson strut front suspension used on many Ford vehicles
L272: 
L273:   * Combustion Chamber
L274: 
L275: Portion of the engine where the air/fuel mixture is ignited and converted to mechanical energy; includes all the space above the piston at top-dead-center (TDC), including the cylinder head, which forms the top of the combustion chamber.
L276: 
L277:   * Command Seating^{™}
L278:     * Front-seat design that is raised higher when compared to a typical seat design
L279:     * Gives the driver and front passenger a "commanding" seating position for comfort and excellent visibility and helps provide drivers a better view of the road due to the raised seat design
L280:     * This is achieved partly by raising the seat's hip pivot point
L281:     * Makes getting into and out of the seats easier
L282:   * Compression Ratio
L283: Ratio between the engine cylinder volume (including the cylinder head volume) when the piston is at the bottom of its stroke and the engine cylinder volume when the piston is at the top of its stroke.
L284: 
L285:   * Connecting Rod
L286:     * Mechanical link between the piston and the crankshaft that enables the piston’s up-and-down travel to be converted into the crankshaft's rotational motion
L287:     * Some Ford engines use forged, powdered-metal, cracked connecting rods. These connecting rods are manufactured using a process pioneered by Ford
L288:     * Connecting rods are typically forged from a flat or round metal billet. Powdered-metal rods, however, begin as loose metal powder blended to the required composition and forged in a form that is nearly at the final "net shape"
L289:   * Constant Velocity (CV) Joint (Front-wheel-drive Vehicles)
L290:     * Refined version of a universal joint, typically used on front-wheel-drive vehicles or rear independent suspensions of rear-wheel-drive vehicles to help reduce vibrations inherent in normal universal joints
L291:     * The CV joint — or double universal joint — cancels out vibrations caused by the transfer of driving power to the wheels
L292:   * Control Arm
L293: 
L294: Suspension element that typically connects a spindle or hub to the frame or body with the use of bushings and/or ball joints.
L295: 
L296:   * Control Trac^{®}
L297: Refer to the 4WD/AWD Operations section of this book for details concerning 4x4 operations.
L298: 
L299:   * Cowl
L300: 
L301: Horizontal portion of the vehicle body behind the engine and immediately to the rear of the hood and under the windshield.
L302: 
L303:   * Crankshaft
L304:     * Primary shaft in the engine that converts the up-and-down motion of the pistons into rotary motion
L305:     * Crankshaft forces the pistons, via the connecting rods, upward to compress the air/fuel mixture prior to combustion. The combustion of the fuel then forces the piston downward, causing the crankshaft to rotate
L306:     * Crankshaft is connected to the flywheel and clutch or torque converter flex plate, which transmits power to the transmission
L307:   * Cross member
L308: Any one of the several horizontal supporting members in a vehicle structure positioned laterally between the side members.
L309: 
L310:   * Cross-Car Beam or Cross cowl Beam
L311: 
L312: Located behind the vehicle dashboard, this feature helps reduce steering wheel movement in the event of a frontal collision and enhances structural rigidity
L313: 
L314:   * Crumple Zones
L315: Sections of a vehicle body and/or frame engineered to progressively deform in a collision, thereby absorbing impact forces instead of transferring them to the passenger compartment. Also known as crush zones.
L316: 
L317:   * Curb Weight
L318: 
L319: Weight of a vehicle with standard equipment, oil, lubricants, coolant and a full tank of fuel. Note: This definition may differ from definitions used by governmental regulatory agencies.
L320: 
L321:   * Cutaway
L322: Incomplete vehicle (based on the Ford E-Series Van) that includes a driver/passenger compartment without a rear wall and is intended for use with specialized conversion bodies.
L323: 
L324:   * Cylinder Head
L325: 
L326: Aluminum or iron casting that houses the top of the intake and exhaust ports and most or all of the valvetrain. It is located directly above the cylinders.
L327: 
L328:   * Cylinders
L329:     * Tubes in an engine block where the pistons move up and down. The number of cylinders and their configurations determine the engine type ("in-line," "V type," etc.)
L330:     * Cylinders are cast into an engine block formed of cast iron or aluminum and then bored and drilled to the final bore diameter
L331: ### D
L332: 
L333:   * Deflection Rate, Spring
L334: 
L335: oad in pounds required to deflect or compress a spring one inch.
L336: 
L337:   * Defroster, Rear-window
L338:     * Feature designed to defog the rear glass quickly and assist in melting snow and ice. Required in some states.
L339:     * Electric rear-window defroster features a silver-filled ceramic heating grid silk-screened on the inside of the glass and includes an instrument panel indicator light and a timer for automatic shutoff

L341:   * Detonation
L342:     * Also known as engine knocking or pre-ignition
L343:     * Detonation is caused by ignition of the air/fuel mixture in the combustion chamber independent of the spark plug firing
L344:     * This condition is an engine malfunction and can often be eliminated by a regular tune-up or use of proper grade fuel
L345:     * See Knock Sensor for more information
L346:   * Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF)
L347:     * Located in the exhaust system after the diesel oxidation catalyst
L348:     * "Scrubs" the particulates in the exhaust gases by trapping them after they have left the combustion chamber
L349:     * Periodically cleans itself through a process known as "regeneration" which is a process similar to a small incinerator that burns off the trapped particles
L350:     * Passive generation burns off soot naturally when exhaust temperatures are high enough
L351:     * Active regeneration (forced burn-off) occurs as needed depending on operational use
L352:   * Differential
L353:     * System of gears in the final drive assembly of a vehicle to transmit torque to the driving wheels regardless of whether the vehicle is moving straight ahead or turning a corner
L354:     * Differential allows the wheels to turn at different speeds while delivering equal torque
L355:     * When cornering, the driving wheel on the inside of the turn travels in a smaller radius than the outside wheel to prevent the outside wheel from dragging in the turn
L356:   * Displacement, Engine
L357: Engine displacement is the measure of the total cylindrical volume through which the pistons of an engine move from one end of the stroke to the other. The formula to determine the displacement of an engine is: Displacement = .7854 x Bore x Bore x Stroke x Number of Cylinders. For example: The displacement of the 4.6L V8 engine is: 280.3 (0.7854 x 3.55 x 3.55 x 3.54 x 8).
